correctness.rationale: The theorem is proved without numerical extrapolation: three-unit-root rigidity forces two dephased modular exponent patterns; CRT identifies the sole allowed 3-adic row valuation r and local p-adic congruence restrictions; exactly 2·3^(a+2r) ordered ternary column triples and p^(b+2k) per other prime power give sigma after division by six. Independent row-stratum counts 3^(3a−2r−3) and p^(3b−2k)−p^(3b−2k−2), with the all-equal boundary p^b, yield the histogram; factoring their weighted sums yields the all-modulus total. Eleven exhaustively enumerated small moduli agree via exact dephased pattern tests.

value.rationale: The first nontrivial odd-cardinality spectral-set problem has a natural precise invariant: how many distinct perfect equal-weight Fourier bases a fixed three-point support admits. The result gives a complete structural histogram and global count for every cyclic order, with prime-power valuation parameters and exact local-to-global factorization. It converts exhaustive pair enumeration into closed arithmetic formulas and explains arithmetic multiplicities; this is stronger than merely rephrasing the known individual-pair test. No broader spectral measure classification is asserted.
